sentences.text: Acristavus is a genus of saurolophine dinosaur whose name translates to "non-crested grandfather," a title reflecting its lack of skull ornamentation compared to nearly all other hadrosaurids.

The holotype specimen, which is the specific fossil the species is based on, includes an almost complete skull along with eleven cervical vertebrae and various limb elements. This animal was a medium-sized duck-billed dinosaur reaching 8.5 meters in length, 2.5 meters in height, and weighing an estimated 2.5 tonnes.
The type species A. gagslarsoni was named in 2011 based on the holotype specimen MOR 1155, which was recovered from the Two Medicine Formation in Teton County, Montana.
A second specimen, UMNHVP 16607, was assigned to Acristavus in 2011 after being excavated from the Wahweap Formation in Utah, a site radiometrically dated between 81 and 76 million years ago.
There are currently two recorded fossil occurrences of Acristavus.

Acristavus shared its environment with dinosaurs including the lambeosaur Adelolophus, the ceratopsian Diabloceratops, ankylosaurs, pachycephalosaurs, and the theropod Lythronax, which was likely the apex predator.
Acristavus is classified within the family Hadrosauridae and belongs to the class Ornithischia.
Gates et al. in 2011 assigned Acristavus to the basal position within the Brachylophosaurini, a tribe consisting of derived members of the Saurolophinae subfamily.

It is debated whether Acristavus and Maiasaura are sister taxa, as Gates concluded they share a relationship, but recent analysis by Prieto-Márquez suggests Maiasaura is more closely related to Brachylophosaurus.

Acristavus lived during a time when the Western Interior Seaway was at its widest, isolating southern Laramidia from the rest of North America, and inhabited an environment containing lakes, floodplains, and east-flowing rivers.
